title: Keyboard operation and focus return
learningObjectives: Explain keyboard operation and focus return and choose an appropriate native HTML interaction.

understand.concept: A modal dialog should support expected keyboard operation, including moving focus into the dialog, keeping interaction within the modal while it is open, and returning focus to the invoking control when it closes. Native dialog methods provide important behaviour, but the content and close controls still need testing.
understand.whyItMatters: Poor focus handling can leave keyboard and screen-reader users disoriented. Ensure there is a visible close action and test Escape behaviour where appropriate for the task.
understand.analogy: Focus is the user's place in the conversation; when a dialog closes, the user should return to the control that opened it.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; actual dialog, disclosure, and focus behaviour follows HTML and accessibility platform rules.

explain.narrative: The native modal dialog manages focus while open; the close event returns focus to the launcher in this example.

practise.guidedTask: Test opening and closing with keyboard only. Verify focus enters the dialog, Escape behaviour is appropriate, and focus returns to the opener.
practise.independentTask: Build an interaction using native HTML first. Test keyboard operation, accessible naming, focus behaviour, and browser support.
hints: Prefer native controls when they meet the requirement.

Test focus entry, dismissal, and return.

questions.prompt: Where should focus normally return after a modal dialog closes?
options: To the control that opened the dialog
questions.answer: To the control that opened the dialog
questions.explanation: Returning focus to the invoker preserves the user's place in the workflow.

questions.prompt: What should guide the choice between native and custom widgets?
options: Whether a native control meets the interaction requirement
Whether a custom widget looks more decorative
Whether ARIA can replace all HTML semantics
questions.answer: Whether a native control meets the interaction requirement
questions.explanation: Native controls are usually the safer choice unless the interaction genuinely requires custom behaviour.
